obligation: G053 -- move to a more compressible member of the same functional basin
method: Boundary snapping toward frequent codes. After q3 group-64 quantization, a weight whose ideal value sits within eps of a cell boundary is reassigned to the neighbouring code WHEN that code is more frequent -- directly buying 'more repeated values' and lower entropy. eps sweeps the size of the near-flat ball the walk is allowed to move in.
objective_as_stated: MINIMIZE DESCRIPTION LENGTH SUBJECT TO NEAR-ZERO FUNCTIONAL CHANGE
bit_conversion: function cost converted to bits via the MEASURED q3->q4 function-space slope (error ratio 0.4224 per bit), so entropy gained and fidelity lost are in the same units and can be netted
verdict: REFUTED AS STATED. There is no near-zero-functional-change regime: the mildest step tested moves 9.5% of weights, buys 0.10-0.11 bits/elem of entropy and costs 7.3-15.1% of the function. Converting both to bits, the entropy gained is almost exactly cancelled by the fidelity lost -- the walk is BREAK-EVEN, not a compression win.
worse_under_the_deployed_route: Even break-even overstates it. G039 refuted entropy coding for this kernel geometry, so under the fixed-width route actually deployed, lower entropy buys ZERO stored bytes while the function damage is real. The walk is a pure loss there.
family_context: This is one basin-walking method. The obligation also names 'more shared structure, better factorization or lower-rank organization' -- G035 refuted cross-layer sharing at matched bits on 3/3 pairs and G034 refuted low-rank at identical bits by 2.93x. The family is consistently negative across three independent methods.
width: four tensors, three depths, MLP only, one walk direction (boundary snapping). A gradient-guided walk along measured flat directions is not tested here.

gradient_guided_member.method: Same move set -- a weight may take its neighbouring code when that code is more frequent -- but ranked by FUNCTIONAL cost rather than by cell-boundary proximity. For y = Wx the output's sensitivity to W[i,j] is proportional to |x_j|, so the cost of a move is (1 - 2|resid|) * scale * ||x_j||, measured on real captured activations. Boundary snapping ranks by |resid| alone and is blind to whether the model uses that column.
gradient_guided_member.verdict: THE OBJECTIVE IS ACHIEVED, and my earlier REFUTED AS STATED was drawn from the weaker member. At the same entropy gain the gradient-guided walk costs 2.5x to 6.8x less function, netting +0.0784 bits/elem against boundary snapping's -0.0206. +2.2% function for 0.116 bits is a defensible reading of 'near-zero functional change'; +15.2% was not.

still_unbankable_here: The win is in DESCRIPTION LENGTH. G039 refuted entropy coding for this kernel geometry, so under the fixed-width route actually deployed, lower entropy buys ZERO stored bytes. The walk now genuinely finds a more compressible member of the basin; this machine cannot spend it.
